The grievance of the petitioners is that a civil dispute between the petitioners and the respondent No. 6 in title suit being TS No. 254/2024, pending for disposal before the learned Civil Judge (Sr.
Division) No. 3, Kamrup (M), is being given Page No.# 3/4 criminal colour.

According to the petitioners, in the meantime, out of the same incident, an FIR was lodged by the wife of the respondent No. 6 i.e. respondent No. 7 before the O/C, Fatashil Ambari Police Station, which is registered as Fatashil Ambari PS case No. 177/2024 under Section 448/ 419/ 420/ 427/ 468/ 471/
380/ 34 IPC.

The respondents on the basis of such FIR forcefully entered in to the disputed property Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam And 6 Ors on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173709328/
2 i.e. the house of the petitioner with the help of police by breaking locks.
2. The FIR primarily relates to illegal occupation of disputed property, which is the subject matter of the title suit.

3. In the aforesaid backdrop, the petitioners represented before the Commissioner of Police,
Kamrup (M) against the O/C and other officials of the Fatashil Ambari Police Station.

Having no alternative, the petitioners have also filed an application before the Director General of Police,
however, of to no avail.
4.
On the direction of this court, a report is submitted.

From the report it is seen that on 11.06.2024,
the respondent no. 7 informed the police that her husband (respondent No. 6) is the owner of the disputed house and they stay at Dimapur.

When they came to visit on 09.06.2024, they found that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 forcefully encroached their house and they illegally occupied the property and also engaged a private security guard and also changed their all CCTV cameras.

5. It is important to note that as per the aforesaid report submitted by S.I. Mintu Baishya of Fatashil Ambari Police Station, on the basis of such information, police entered into the house, broke the lock of the doors, went to the 2 nd floor of the house and found one Paresh Dey and his wife and said Paresh Dey introduced himself as the manager of one Harish Parikh.
Accordingly, Fatashil Ambari PS case No. 177/2024 under Section 448/419/420/427/468/471/380/34 IPC was registered and investigation has been completed and charge-sheet has been filed on 20.01.2025.
6. Thus, from the report, prima-facie, it appears that on the allegation of illegal occupation of a property, the police entered into the premises and broke the lock of the premises.
In the aforesaid backdrop, prima-facie, in the opinion of this Page No.# 4/4 court, suggestive of excess by police.
7. Issue notice, returnable on 14.05.2025.
8. Mr. S Baruah, learned State counsel accepts notices on behalf of respondent Nos. 1 to 5.
Petitioners to take steps for service of notice upon the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 by way of registered post with A/D and by usual process within a period of one week from today.

9. A copy of the report submitted by Mr. Mintu Baishya, S.I. of Fatashil Ambari be brought on record by an affidavit by the respondent No. 5.
10.
The petitioner is permitted to implead the aforesaid Mintu Baishya, S.I. of Fatashil Ambari Police Station as a party respondent in this case.
11. Accordingly, amended cause title be furnished before the Registry and after acceptance of the same, the amended cause title be furnished to the respondents.

12. Issue notice to the newly respondent, returnable on 14.05.2025.
